content:
We have a list of templates returned. Need to find the one that corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation (acyl chloride + aromatic, halide broken). The description: halide functional group is gone, carbon-chlorine bond broken, new C-C bond formed. So template should have Cl attached to aromatic in reactants and carbonyl attached in product.

Look at each entry's mapped_rxn. The first entry (reaction_id 1282789) seems to involve Cl attached to aromatic and carbonyl etc. Let's examine its mapped_rxn: It's long. It shows product with ...[Cl:24] etc. The reactant includes ...Cl... So likely Friedel-Crafts acylation.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The search result includes reaction_id, template_hash, but not template_id. Possibly template_id is the reaction_id? Actually template_id is integer. In other tasks, they used template_id as the integer ID of the template (maybe reaction_id?). The search result fields: reaction_id, template_hash, retro_smarts_template, canonical_smarts_template, mapped_rxn, etc. Likely template_id corresponds to reaction_id? Or there is separate template ID not shown. The prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash) as an integer". In search results, reaction_id is integer. So we can use reaction_id as template_id.

Thus choose the appropriate entry. Need to ensure it's Friedel-Crafts acylation. Look at entry 1282789: The reactant_smiles includes "...Cl[c:12]1[c:11]([C:9]([NH:8][c:7]2... )=[O:10])..." So aromatic with Cl attached. The product_smiles includes ...[Cl:24] still? Actually product has Cl attached to aromatic? product_smiles: ...[Cl:24] appears inside. Wait product still has Cl? That seems not broken. Might be different.

Check entry 1419102: reactant includes Cl... product maybe not? product_smiles includes ...[Cl:46] etc. Not.

We need a template where halide is removed (Cl leaves) and carbonyl attaches. Look at entry 232393: reactant_smiles: "Cl[CH2:7][c:6]1..." product_smiles: no Cl? product has ...[Cl:46] still. Not.

Entry 1341356: reactant includes Cl attached to aromatic? yes "Cl[c:9]1n..." product includes ...[Cl:18] still.

Entry 1035472: reactant includes "Cl-[CH2...]" product includes ...Cl? product has ...Cl? product_smiles includes ...Cl? It has ...[Cl:8] in product? Actually product_smiles: ...[Cl:8] present. Not.

Entry 241287 similar.

Entry 1363675: reactant includes "Cl[C:7]..." product includes ...Cl? product has ...Cl? product_smiles includes ...[Cl:22] still.

Thus maybe the first entry 1282789 is the correct Friedel-Crafts acylation where Cl is on aromatic and carbonyl attached. But product still has Cl? product_smiles includes ...[Cl:24] inside aromatic? Actually product_smiles: ...[Cl:24] appears attached to aromatic ring (maybe the acyl chloride's Cl remains on carbonyl? In Friedel-Crafts acylation, the acyl chloride loses Cl, forming acyl cation, Cl becomes Cl- (not attached). So product should not have Cl attached to aromatic. The template may involve Cl attached to aromatic as leaving group? Wait typical Friedel-Crafts acylation: aromatic + RCOCl -> aromatic-CO-R + HCl. The Cl is on acyl carbon, not aromatic. So the bond broken is C-Cl of acyl chloride, not aromatic halide. The description says "breaking a carbon-chlorine bond". Could be the acyl chloride's C-Cl bond broken. So the template should have Cl attached to carbonyl carbon in reactant, not aromatic. The product will have carbonyl attached to aromatic, no Cl.

Thus look for template where reactant includes "C(=O)Cl" attached to aromatic? In entry 1282789 reactant includes "...C(=O)Cl" attached to aromatic? Yes reactant_smiles includes "...C(=O)Cl" attached to aromatic ring (Cl on carbonyl). product_smiles includes ...[Cl:24] still? Wait product_smiles includes ...[Cl:24] attached to aromatic? Actually product_smiles: ...[Cl:24] appears inside aromatic ring? Let's parse: product_smiles: '[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][c:4]1[cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([NH:8][C:9](=[O:10])[c:11]2[c:12]([NH:13][CH2:14][c:15]3[cH:16][cH:17][cH:18][cH:19][cH:20]3)[n:21][n:22][c:23]([Cl:24])[cH:25]2)[cH:26][cH:27]1'

Yes product still has Cl attached to heterocycle (maybe part of the original acyl chloride? Actually the Cl is attached to the heterocycle not aromatic). So not correct.

Maybe there is a template not in list? Could be we need to search with different criteria. Use functional_groups_broken: ["acyl_chloride"]? Not available. Could search with bonds_broken: ["C-Cl"] and bonds_formed: ["C-C"] but need correct format: bond types are atomic numbers? In earlier error, format expects "6-17" etc. Need to know which atoms correspond. Hard.

Alternative: Use search without bond criteria, just functional_groups_broken ["halide"] maybe returns many. Could filter manually for Friedel-Crafts acylation by checking mapped_rxn for pattern "Cl" on carbonyl in reactant and not in product.

Let's iterate through results and find one where reactant has "C(=O)Cl" and product does not have Cl. Look at each entry's reactant_smiles and product_smiles.

Entry 1282789: reactant has "...C(=O)Cl" yes. product also has Cl attached to heterocycle, not carbonyl. So Cl still present but maybe on different position. Not ideal.

Entry 1419102: reactant includes "...Cl" on aromatic? product includes Cl as well.

Entry 232393: reactant includes "Cl[CH2]" not carbonyl.

Entry 1341356: reactant includes "Cl[c:9]" not carbonyl.

Entry 1035472: reactant includes "Cl-[CH2]" not carbonyl.

Entry 241287 similar.

Entry 1363675: reactant includes "Cl[C:7]" attached to carbonyl? It is "Cl[C:7]([c:6]... )=[O:8]" that's carbonyl carbon attached to Cl (acyl chloride). product includes Cl still attached to carbonyl? product has ...[Cl:22] attached to aromatic? Actually product_smiles includes ...[Cl:22] attached to aromatic ring (maybe same). So not.

Thus maybe none of these are Friedel-Crafts acylation. Could be need to search with functional_groups_formed ["carbonyl"] and broken ["halide"]? Let's try search again with functional_groups_formed ["carbonyl"] maybe.
